messages:
maya: Heads-up — proposing we change rerank endpoint cost model to separate candidate_units from token_units. Fanout (number of candidates dispatched) should be accounted for independently from token cost. Thoughts?
ben: Can you sketch the billing/quota math? today everything maps to tokens which hides concurrency impact. Small token calls with huge fanout kill throughput.
maya: Short sketch: 
1) charge_units = token_units + candidate_units_weighted
2) candidate_units_weighted = max(num_candidates * model_cost_factor, kv_cache_credit)
3) add per-request hints + server-side max_fanout enforcement

Example request: 
```
POST /v1/rerank
{ "candidates": [...], "model": "rwd-compact-3b", "fanout_hint": 128 }
```

alex: `fanout_hint` name bikesheds me. Maybe `desired_topk` or `client_max_fanout`? Also we already have per-tenant concurrency quotas — are we introducing per-request caps or just accounting?
maya: Both. Accounting for cost + optional per-request shape enforcement. We should let tenants set a soft per-request cap in console that maps to routing shaping (e.g., truncate or sample candidates).
juniper: Console UX notes: expose a cost estimator that shows token vs fanout impact, and surface which model variant was chosen per-run. Operators want ability to simulate cost for different fanout numbers.
sarah: Also think about streaming/partial scoring semantics. If we stream candidate batches back to client, scoring normalization matters. What's our canonical score wire format? floats in [0,1]? logit?
ben: Implementation detail we've discussed before: persist two values in telemetry — raw_logit (float32) for model signals and normalized_score (float32 0..1) for API responses. That keeps both fidelity for offline evals and consistent API shape.
ops: infra-bot: deploy scheduled — rerank-fanout-quota-proposal will land on staging 2026-03-25T09:00Z. :rocket:
maya: Next steps: I'll draft proto changes for RerankRequest (add `client_max_fanout` and `fanout_hint`), update quota calc in routing service, and add telemetry fields (fanout, chosen_variant, model_cost_factor).
alex: Please add compatibility: if no fanout fields present we fall back to legacy token-only accounting. Also add unit tests that assert identical billing for legacy requests.
juniper: Add console opt-in toggle to flip on new fanout-aware billing per org for canary. We should not surprise GA customers.
maya: Open questions I'll add to the PR/RFC: a) exact weight factor per model class (gpu-hours proxy) b) enforcement semantics during canary (soft vs hard) c) telemetry sampling thresholds to avoid noise d) how KV-cache hits reduce candidate_units.
ben: One more: routing policy should prefer lower-cost model variants when requested fanout > threshold. Add `model_affinity_hint` in routing proto so product can say "prefer smaller models for wide fanout".
maya: Great. I'll include that. Filing PR and RFC today — will tag reviewers. :raised_hands:
alex: LGTM — ping me for proto review and quota calc verification.
juniper: I'll design console mockups after the RFC lands.
maya: Thanks all. Will follow up with PR link. :+1:
